sample: Bulwark release 0.35 implements 16 defense-in-depth controls against payment fraud, prompt injection, and supply-chain tampering, all validated through laboratory simulation and live model testing.

Critical payment controls—invoice binding, payee registry confirmation, and approval pinning—have been measured in both simulated and live conditions, blocking unauthorized transfers before execution.
Prompt injection defenses include MCP tool description pinning, skill and plugin lock enforcement, and a sandbox for model-written code, all exercised against live Haiku 4.5 model runs.

Integrity and auditability are secured through a sealed evidence chain with tamper detection, task-scoped identity tokens, and incident containment gates that enforce mandatory deadline and owner fields.
Runtime safety is enforced via per-task budget counters that prevent loops and fan-out, egress allow-lists that block unlisted domains, and memory trust labels that prevent cross-tenant poisoning.
Detection of attacks that penetrated other layers found 25 of 36 simulated payment fraud cases; mutation testing on unit tests identifies gaps in authority-path coverage.
All controls are production-ready for deployment with the understanding that live effectiveness validation against real-world attack patterns will continue post-launch.

sample: Bulwark release 0.35 has been tested and measured in simulation across sixteen control areas covering payment integrity, code execution, and incident response.
Controls against prompt injection threats have been measured with a live model in a simulated tenant, including description pinning for MCP tools, prompt release gating, and skill and plugin locking.
Payment controls have been measured in simulation: changed bank accounts are held until confirmation, payments are bound to invoices and payees, and approval changes require new approvals.
Egress controls have been measured both in simulation and with a live model to block unlisted domains and invented recipients.
Evidence chain integrity has been measured in simulation to detect edit, delete, rechain and truncate operations.
Code execution is constrained by per-task budgets, runtime scope limits, task-scoped identity tokens, and sandbox restrictions with no network access.
The detection layer found 25 of 36 simulated attack payments, with 31 false alerts.
OPEN ITEM: all measurements are from a simulated tenant with no production data.
OPEN ITEM: live model testing was limited to one model.
OPEN ITEM: OWASP and NIST alignment requires verification.
